title: Composing in his head and hearing tunes by ear
summary: He wrote tunes quickly on paper, trumpet and mostly in his head, a skill from whistling minstrel tunes he'd heard only once.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You were talking before about Yacht Club Swing piece, your piece, had you been writing very much along down through the years?

Hmmm, well yes and no. I've had -- oh, I at one time, one time when I had so many things, and after Yacht Club, and band, before I got disgusted and said to hell with them, threw them away and forgot about it, because at that time, how good they were, I do not know, and fifteen or twenty minutes I could write a tune. I mean, and idea would come to me (snaps fingers) and I could hear it, and maybe put it on paper, and play it.
How -- did you write, or did you compose on the piano, on the trumpet, or on paper?

Yeah, and mainly in my head, because I learned, I think I learned that when I was quite young, because as I told you, I used to listen to the minstrel bands, and hear them play, and I hadn't never heard the tune before, so
I was standing there listening to them play, remember it, whistle it until I got home, and play it.

And in a way I can still do that, you know? That's how good -- keen my ear was, I guess. And that's very important. In music -- I wouldn't say jazz only -- in music, is being able to play what you hear, being able to hear. A lot of people, they say they can't carry a tune in a basket. That's why. You know. You can't -- if you can't hear the thing, I mean you -- well forget it.
After you got home and played it, then did you write it down? Or did you just depend on --
No, no. Once I played it, and seemed to create a -- the thing that I'd already had then, and I would never forget it.
